summary: Budget-finished breadth pass: 232 inherited whole nodes retained and 71 declaration-sized targets added (303 total). The four previously absent reserved keys now have mathematical carriers, scope-qualified APIs and discriminating tests: scheme Brauer groups, coherent Grothendieck duality, equivariant sheaf cohomology and Galois gerbs. All implementations remain unchecked; proof/carrier gaps and SF.0–SF.6 remaining targets are explicit. Complete describes this pass, not stage closure or formalisation.

nodes.title: Residue-preserving étale neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: For a commutative R and ideal I, an object is an existing CommAlgCat R algebra B satisfying Algebra.Etale R B and bijectivity of the canonical quotientMap R/I → B/(I.map(algebraMap R B)). Neighbourhood I is the existing full subcategory on this predicate; its morphisms are every actual R-algebra map. An arbitrary abstract isomorphism of quotients is not sufficient.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity, including the zero ring; I is an arbitrary ideal unless a stronger hypothesis is explicitly stated. Ring carriers and target rings may be placed in a common universe.
proofSteps: Instantiate Ideal.quotientMap with Ideal.le_comap_map; this fixes the reduction map, rather than choosing a residue-field equivalence.
Use ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory and its inclusion, retaining all algebra maps, including distinct parallel maps with identical reduction.
The identity R-algebra is an object. A localization R[1/x] is an object when x becomes a unit in R/I: it is already etale and its quotient localization is R/I.
Tensor and parallel-map operations are supplied by the following separate nodes. No scheme, etale, ideal, tensor or full-subcategory carrier is rebuilt.
acceptance: Inverting 2 over (Z,(5)) qualifies; inverting 5 does not.
The diagonal Z/5 → (Z/5)^2 is not bijective, so the two-sheeted etale product is rejected.

nodes.title: Tensor products give common targets
nodes.statement: If B and C are etale R-algebras with canonical quotient R/I, then B tensor_R C is etale over R and its canonical quotient by I is R/I. The standard tensor inclusions give a common target in Neighbourhood I.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity, including the zero ring; I is an arbitrary ideal unless a stronger hypothesis is explicitly stated. Ring carriers and target rings may be placed in a common universe.
proofSteps: Base change Algebra.Etale R C to B, then compose with Algebra.Etale R B.
Use the existing quotient/tensor equivalences to identify (B tensor_R C)/I with (B/IB) tensor_(R/I) (C/IC).
Use the two canonical reduction isomorphisms to identify this tensor product with R/I. Check the resulting map is the canonical quotientMap, not just some ring equivalence.
Lift both existing tensor algebra maps to the full subcategory.
acceptance: For I=top all reductions are zero; the construction still applies.
For two copies of R[1/2] at (Z,(5)), the common target is again canonically R[1/2].

nodes.title: Parallel algebra maps can be equalized
nodes.statement: For every f,g:B→C in Neighbourhood I there exist D in Neighbourhood I and h:C→D with h∘f=h∘g. No assumption that f=g, that maps are inclusions, or that the category is thin is allowed.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity, including the zero ring; I is an arbitrary ideal unless a stronger hypothesis is explicitly stated. Ring carriers and target rings may be placed in a common universe.
proofSteps: Form E=C tensor_(B,f,g) C, and its structure as a quotient of C tensor_R C. Then form D=E tensor_(C tensor_R C) C using multiplication into the last C.
Each B→C map is etale by the existing of_restrictScalars theorem. Base change and composition show R→D is etale.
Reduce this iterated tensor diagram modulo I. All object reductions are canonically R/I and all reduced morphisms are identities, so D/ID is canonically R/I.
The map C→D equalizes f,g by the tensor balancing equations. This is the actual source coequalizer construction; native scalar-tower transport remains a recorded implementation gap.
acceptance: Over R=Z/6,I=(3), C=F3×F2×F2 admits distinct identity and sheet-swap endomorphisms. Projection to F3 equalizes them and remains a neighbourhood.
The sheet-swap witness rejects a plan that replaces this category by a directed poset of embeddings.

nodes.title: Henselization of a ring and ideal
nodes.statement: Import the general arbitrary-pair henselization from PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselisation-of-pairs as the single carrier. Its concrete Mathlib-only presentation H is the colimit in CommAlgCat R of the étale neighbourhood inclusion reindexed by equivSmallModel; η:R→H is algebraMap and IH=I.map η. This reserved key reexports that carrier and its canonical presentation/API comparisons; it does not plan an independent henselization or assume H is a completion.
hypotheses: All rings are commutative with identity, including the zero ring; I is an arbitrary ideal unless a stronger hypothesis is explicitly stated. Ring carriers and target rings may be placed in a common universe.
proofSteps: Use the actual neighbourhood full subcategory and its essential-smallness proof.
Define diagram I=(equivSmallModel (Neighbourhood I)).inverse followed by the full-subcategory inclusion.

Present the imported P3 carrier using existing CommAlgCat colimits. The displayed H=colimit(diagram I) is a concrete prototype of that same colimit; transport along the canonical colimit equivalence, preserving unit, ideal and residue maps. It is not a second construction.
Use the universal cocone to obtain all stage maps. The following nodes establish canonical residue preservation, Jacobson containment, simple-root lifting and the initial property.
Treat diagram, extended ideal, reduction map and stage maps as routine instantiations of existing categorical/algebra operations. They do not redefine ind-etaleness or assume H is the completion.

The exact existing P3 node supplies the general colimit, universal property and its flatness/power-quotient/Noetherian/completion/filtered-colimit interfaces. Their detailed formal proofs and canonical presentation comparison remain open there and here; do not re-plan them as a second carrier. Any future ownership transfer requires the recorded rescope decision.
acceptance: At I=0, H is canonically R; at I=top, H is the zero R-algebra.
Already henselian pairs are fixed. For F5 at its zero maximal ideal the residue field remains F5, not its separable closure.

nodes.title: Ideal membership is detected at a later neighbourhood
nodes.statement: For b in a stage B, stage_B(b) belongs to IH if and only if there are a later stage C and one arrow t:B→C with diagram(t)(b) in IC. The existential is over actual neighbourhood arrows, not an inclusion order or an embedding of carriers.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring with identity, including the zero ring; I is any ideal, without finite-generation, Noetherian, local or completeness assumptions.
B and C are objects of the chosen small neighbourhood diagram. All carrier rings lie in a common universe; its transition maps need not be injective.
proofSteps: Transport filteredness to SmallModel by IsFiltered.of_equivalence. To apply Concrete.colimit_exists_rep and colimit_rep_eq_iff_exists to diagram I, compose commAlgCatEquivUnder with Under.forget and the commutative-ring forgetful functor: the equivalence preserves colimits, Under.forget preserves connected colimits by IsFiltered.isConnected, and the latter functor preserves filtered colimits. Identify this composite with the actual CommAlgCat forgetful functor using the natural isomorphism and preservesColimit_of_natIso. These are built generic inputs, not a new colimit construction.

Unfold Ideal.map as the span of η(I). Submodule.span_induction proves that each member has a witness built from finitely many generators η(r), r in I, and finitely many coefficients in H. Represent those coefficients using Concrete.colimit_exists_rep and use IsFiltered.sup_exists to move them to one stage C0. Their finite sum lies in IC0 and has the prescribed image in H.

For the given b, detect the equality between its stage image and the finite-sum image using Concrete.colimit_rep_eq_iff_exists. Refine C0 and B, retaining a single arrow from B; finite parallel-arrow discrepancies are equalized using sup_exists. This yields diagram(t)(b) in IC.

Conversely, stage_C maps IC into IH because its R-algebra map commutes with η. Apply Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap and the existing cocone naturality. No finite generating set for the whole ideal and no injectivity are used.

nodes.title: A monic polynomial descends to a neighbourhood
nodes.statement: For every monic f in H[T], there are a small stage B and a monic p in B[T] with coefficient map stage_B sending p exactly to f. No injectivity of stage_B, prescribed degree of p, or finite-generation condition on I is asserted.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring with identity, including the zero ring; I is any ideal, without finite-generation, Noetherian, local or completeness assumptions.
B and C are objects of the chosen small neighbourhood diagram. All carrier rings lie in a common universe; its transition maps need not be injective.
proofSteps: Use Polynomial.Monic.as_sum to write f=X^n plus the finite sum of its coefficients of exponents below n. The representation also holds for H a subsingleton ring.

Represent the finitely many lower coefficients by Concrete.colimit_exists_rep. IsFiltered.sup_exists moves their representatives to a single stage B; for an empty coefficient family use the nonempty neighbourhood category.
Define p at B by the same X^n plus lower-coefficient sum. Its leading term gives monicity (or use the subsingleton convention if B is zero). Mapping coefficients returns f term by term.

This construction chooses the leading coefficient to be 1 at B, rather than claiming an arbitrary polynomial lift must be monic. Do not infer degree equality through a non-injective or zero-target ring map.
acceptance: The polynomial 1 uses an empty lower-coefficient list and still has a stage representative.
A monic polynomial over the zero colimit ring is allowed; the statement makes no unjustified degree-preservation claim.

nodes.title: A quotient unit descends to a later neighbourhood
nodes.statement: If b is in a stage B and its image in H/IH is a unit, then there are a later stage C and an arrow t:B→C such that the class of diagram(t)(b) in C/IC is a unit. No lift of that unit is asserted to be a unit in B or in H.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring with identity, including the zero ring; I is any ideal, without finite-generation, Noetherian, local or completeness assumptions.
B and C are objects of the chosen small neighbourhood diagram. All carrier rings lie in a common universe; its transition maps need not be injective.
proofSteps: Choose an inverse of the class of stage_B(b) in H/IH and a representative c in H, using quotient surjectivity. The inverse equation says stage_B(b)c−1 belongs to IH.

Represent c at a stage and take a common target with B using Concrete.colimit_exists_rep and IsFiltered.sup_exists. Its product-minus-one has the required stage image by the ring-map laws and cocone naturality.
Apply mem_extended_iff_exists_stage to that one product-minus-one. At the later target its class is zero, so the transported b and c have product 1 in C/IC.
The quotient is commutative, so the same c gives the two-sided inverse and hence a unit. No henselian-pair theorem, residue-comparison result, or base-ring unit hypothesis is used, avoiding a cycle.

nodes.title: Simple-root data descend simultaneously
nodes.statement: Let f in H[T] be monic and a0 in H satisfy f(a0) in IH and f′(a0) invertible modulo IH. There exist a small neighbourhood B, a monic p in B[T], and b in B such that coefficient mapping sends p to f, stage_B(b)=a0, p(b) belongs to IB, and p′(b) is invertible in B/IB. Every condition holds at the same stage.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring with identity, including the zero ring; I is any ideal, without finite-generation, Noetherian, local or completeness assumptions.
B and C are objects of the chosen small neighbourhood diagram. All carrier rings lie in a common universe; its transition maps need not be injective.
proofSteps: First use exists_stage_monic_polynomial for f and Concrete.colimit_exists_rep for a0; pass to a common neighbourhood by sup_exists. Polynomial.Monic.map preserves the monic representative, and cocone naturality preserves its exact coefficient map and the approximate root's image.
By Polynomial.eval_map_apply, the stage image of p(b) is f(a0). Apply mem_extended_iff_exists_stage and transport p and b along the resulting arrow to obtain the actual membership p(b) in IB.
Use Polynomial.derivative_map together with eval_map_apply to identify the transported derivative's stage image with f′(a0). Apply exists_stage_quotient_unit and transport p and b once more.

Polynomial.Monic.map and ordinary ideal-map containment preserve all previously attained conditions under the last refinement. Recheck the two exact image equalities by cocone naturality. Thus the standard-étale presentation uses finite-stage coefficients and its actual residue section, not a new postulated descent field.
acceptance: For f=T²−1 over F5 and a0=1, the root condition holds and the derivative is 2, a quotient unit.
For the same f and a0 over F2, the derivative is zero in the nonzero residue field, so this lemma's invertibility hypothesis fails.
Finite ideal-sum witnesses suffice even when the original ideal has infinitely many generators.

Since C is a neighbourhood, its canonical R/I→C/IC is injective; hence r belongs to I. This identifies the kernel of the actual reducedMap and proves its injectivity.

nodes.title: An étale section selects an idempotent component
nodes.statement: For an etale R-algebra B and actual R-algebra section sigma:B→R, there exists e in B with e²=e, sigma(e)=1 and e*b=e*algebraMap(R,B)(sigma(b)) for every b. This fixes the actual section rather than merely asserting an abstract product.
hypotheses: R and B are commutative rings with identity, including the zero ring; B is an R-algebra. Etaleness is required only for the selector, product and localization existence statements, not the kernel adapter. All carriers lie in a common universe.
proofSteps: Equip R with the B-algebra structure sigma.toAlgebra and prove the R/B/R scalar tower from sigma.comp_algebraMap. The section is surjective since sigma(algebraMap r)=r.

Use FormallyEtale.of_restrictScalars and iff_of_surjective to make ker(sigma) an idempotent ideal. FinitePresentation.ker_fG_of_surjective supplies finite generation; choose its idempotent generator k using Ideal.isIdempotentElem_iff_of_fg.

Set e=1-k. Then sigma(k)=0 gives sigma(e)=1 and k²=k gives e²=e. For each b, b-algebraMap(sigma(b)) belongs to ker(sigma), so it is c*k. Multiplication by 1-k kills it and proves the exact selection equation.
The current native proof uses only built pinned declarations; the generic unramified diagonal product is already built and is not a new planned construction.

api.name: TauCeti.SchemeFoundations.IdealPullback.sheafCompNatIso_assoc
api.statement: For arbitrary f:X→Y,g:Y→Z,h:Z→W and I on W, first comparing (f followed by g),h and then f,g for I.comap h equals: transport along scheme-morphism associativity, compare f,(g followed by h), then transport comap_comp(g,h) after comap f. nodes.title: Quasi-coherent sheaf of algebras
nodes.statement: For a native scheme X, an associative unital O_X-algebra is a sheaf of rings A with a central structure map O_X→A. Require its underlying O_X-module to be quasi-coherent. Morphisms are unital sheaf-ring maps preserving the central structure map. The carrier is not a sheaf of commutative algebras: matrix algebras must be allowed.
hypotheses: X is a scheme; algebra sheaves are associative unital with central O_X scalars. Matrix degrees and stabilizing bundle ranks are positive; impose connectedness or quasi-compactness only where stated.
proofSteps: Use native sheaves and O_X-modules. Specify multiplication, unit and their sheaf compatibility, with the scalar image central.
The noncommutative algebra-object/tensor and pullback implementation is a recorded carrier gap; do not substitute commutative algebras or a proposition-valued witness.

nodes.title: Azumaya algebra on a scheme
nodes.statement: A quasi-coherent O_X-algebra A is Azumaya when there is a surjective étale covering U_i→X and O_{U_i}-algebra isomorphisms f_i* A≅Mat_{d_i}(O_{U_i}), with d_i≥1. This implies finite locally free and faithful underlying module. Degree is locally constant; no single global degree is required.

proofSteps: Use étale-local matrix splittings on the native scheme étale site.
Relate the finite-projective, faithful and enveloping-endomorphism criterion to this definition on affine opens; that comparison is an explicit lemma, not definitional equality.

nodes.title: Scheme Brauer group

nodes.title: Coherent Grothendieck duality

nodes.title: Semilinear equivariant sheaf

nodes.title: Acyclicity for the composite section functor
nodes.statement: For an injective equivariant O_X-module sheaf I, its global-section Γ-module is acyclic for invariants. Obtain this by a retract of the sections of a coinduced sheaf; no exactness of the free O_X-module left adjoint to abelian-group sections is assumed.
hypotheses: Γ is a discrete, possibly infinite group acting by ringed-space automorphisms. Sheaves are O_X-modules with semilinear action over that base action; support subsets are Γ-stable.
proofSteps: The forgetful functor to ordinary O_X-module sheaves is exact. Its right adjoint coinduction is the product of the pullbacks by the base automorphisms; the identity component detects monomorphisms.

Embed the underlying sheaf of I in an ordinary injective sheaf J. Adjunction gives a monomorphism I→Coind(J), split because I is equivariantly injective. Consequently Γ(X,I) is a retract of Γ(X,Coind(J)).

Global sections commute with products and identify the latter Γ-module with the coinduced module Map(Γ,Γ(X,J)). Establish its invariants-acyclicity by the contracting group-cochain resolution, then pass to the retract. These category, section and resolution comparisons remain explicit open proof leaves.
The previous constant/free-sheaf argument is false in this generality: on a point with O_X=F_p, tensoring the injection p:Z→Z with O_X gives the zero endomorphism of F_p.

nodes.title: Galois gerbs
nodes.statement: Fix a characteristic-zero field k, a Galois extension k′/k inside an algebraic closure, and Γ=Gal(k′/k) with its Krull topology. A gerb consists of a linear algebraic group H/k′ and a topological extension 1→H(k′)→E→Γ→1 with discrete kernel. Every lift of σ acts on the kernel through an algebraic σ-semilinear automorphism of H. Over Gal(k′/K) for some finite K/k inside k′, there is a local splitting chart whose algebraic conjugation action is effective descent to K. None of these conditions forces a global splitting.
hypotheses: For the topological prefix use groups with the stated topologies and a discrete kernel. Algebraic gerbs additionally use a characteristic-zero field and a Galois extension with its Krull topology, linear algebraic kernels and effective algebraic local descent.
proofSteps: Use the native group extension for kernel points and the existing scheme group objects for H.
Supply algebraic semilinear isomorphisms and their agreement with conjugation on points; local effective descent is actual algebraic descent data, not a continuity-only substitute.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv1912.03657v4 AppendixA.2 physical/printed81, arbitrary-open section equality and ensuing flabbiness proof; rendered page inspected
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts, for any open U, that Gamma-invariant sections of p-inverse(I) over q-inverse(U) coincide with invariant sections of I over p(q-inverse(U)). It also claims flabbiness for the sheaf descended from an equivariant injective I.

sourceIssues.reason: Take X a point, Gamma=Z and I=Map(Z,Q/Z) with translation. It is the coinduction of the injective abelian group Q/Z and hence an injective Gamma-module. validationBoundary.sourceRead: Selected primary locators recorded separately from inherited provenance. Stacks displayed statements/proofs/comments, Kisin §3.1.1–3.1.2, and Kings–Sprang arXiv v4 Appendix A were read; recursive proof leaves are not claimed read. Every revised API/test/comment was checked. Selected primary scope and proof frontiers are recorded in the review report.

restructure.detail: The full existing PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselisation-of-pairs node plans the general arbitrary ring/ideal colimit and left-adjoint property, overlapping the exact reserved key assigned by #642. Its API also contains flatness, all ideal-power quotients, Noetherianity, completion and filtered-colimit comparisons. These are requirements to reconcile, not new definitions to copy.
restructure.proposal: Keep SchemeAndStackFoundations:key/henselization as the single general carrier and refinement owner required by the key survey; retain the fifteen current refinement IDs. Preserve PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselisation-of-pairs as a compatibility/import node, using the reserved key and its declaration-sized outputs and keeping the flatness, ideal-power, Noetherian, completion and filtered-colimit requirements as imports or source-decomposed outputs owned once. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology retains the f-adic topology/continuity/plus-ring specialization using that carrier. Route dependencies at node granularity to avoid dragging adic/Perfectoid theory into SF.0; validate any needed substage split before applying stage links. This proposal is unaccepted and does not modify either supplier packet.

restructure.detail: RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/15 (confirmed): the only atlas input of SF.5 is SF.4 (deformation, formal schemes, algebraization, alterations), which Chow groups, Gysin maps, Chern classes, Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch, surface Riemann–Roch and the Hodge index theorem do not use. RS-25 also forwarded R11.1, R11.3 and StableReduction Layers 7–9 into SF.5, so SF.5 and its consumers inherit Néron-model, abelian-scheme, p-divisible-group and adic-space ancestors. SF.5’s real inputs are curve Riemann–Roch and adjunction (SF.3), projective and flag bundles with O(1) (AlgebraicModuli R09.1), coherent duality on smooth projective surfaces (SF.2 key/coherent-duality, reaching SF.5 through SF.3) and arithmetic-surface intersections (StableReduction Layer 4). The edge SF.4 → SF.5 also blocks SF.4 from importing StableReductionPartII MC.4, which requires SF.5.
restructure.proposal: Replace SF.4 → SF.5 by SF.3 → SF.5 and AlgebraicModuli R09.1 → SF.5; keep StableReduction Layer 4 → SF.5. Delete the RS-25 forwarding links R11.1 → SF.5, R11.3 → SF.5 and StableReduction Layers 7, 8 and 9 → SF.5. Add SF.4 → AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5 and SF.4 → PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.5 (RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/16, RT-AREA-etale/21), and StableReductionPartII MC.2 → SF.4 (RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/17). These changes are acyclic in the current assembled atlas with promoted blueprints and research roadmap definitions, checked 2026-10-09. Defer MC.4 → SF.4: removing SF.4 → SF.5 is insufficient in that graph. It still has SF.4 → DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.5 → PerfectoidQuotients Q3 → Q4 → AdicEtaleGeometry A3 → RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:integral-Y → VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB0 → AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 → PELModuli M2 → M6 → StableReductionPartII MC.4. Attach the projective-cover request only to the schematic alteration nodes and split/reroute the formal and cohomological consumers before considering any whole-stage edge. The broader unreviewed research packets also have the PrismaticCohomology PR.1 path described by the fixer; check all these routes at node granularity when implementing the supplier split. This proposal edits no other packet or atlas file.
